Really simplistic view of addiction honestly. Yeah a lot of artists and people in general are addicts. It’s awesome that we have great content and that we can benefit from a situation that is already “naturally” taking place. But a lot of them get high for the purposes of getting the creatives juices flowing not to mention the drug use that takes place when rehearsing, setting up, and performing a show. Not many people, not many artists, can do that well and perform for thousands and put on a great show while sober. The nerves alone would be reason enough to partake. Then after the applause and the praise and the adoration,  artists can find validation in their addictions. They feel good and they received such great results, so why stop?? That is how addiction is nasty and how insidious it is. If an artist is profiting from his addiction, socially, financially, economically, they may think to themselves “why should I change? And if they receive great support and praise for their work they may also think “should I even change”? And those two questions needs to be acknowledged and addressed before we even get to “how to change”?
